facets.text: He contrasts mass-market electric cars, which he says would have happened without him, with a space-faring civilization, which he says is not inevitable.

Shuttle retirement left the US unable to send people to orbit in the period being described. The book dates his post-PayPal-sale inquiry to 2001; that chronology is preserved as given, not independently verified.

Expected Moon/Mars bases and space hotels contrasted with actual progress in a pocket-sized device giving worldwide information and communication; progress in one field did not establish progress in space.

The initial aim was not to create a company but to create a will to explore; he explicitly says this diagnosis was wrong. People had not lost the will, but did not see a way forward and would not keep futilely pushing against a wall.

He reports that support appeared once people realized there was a way to do it. He places this in a specifically US exploration narrative, calling exploration fundamental to that psyche, rather than demonstrating a universal cultural claim.
